summary:
Fixed and verified.

**The needle:** `RateLimiter.getClientIp()` in `app/app/ratelimiter.ts` used the client-controlled `X-Forwarded-For` header as the rate-limit key. Since a client can set that header to any value, an attacker just rotates it (`10.0.0.1`, `10.0.0.2`, …) to land in a fresh bucket on every request — bypassing the limiter completely.

**The fix:** Key rate limiting on the actual TCP socket peer address (`req.socket.remoteAddress`), which the client cannot spoof. The header should only ever be trusted when it demonstrably comes from a trusted proxy on a trusted network, which isn't the case here.

**Test results:** Both checks pass — the limiter blocks excess normal requests (10 pass / 5 blocked) and now holds firm under header spoofing (10 pass / 20 blocked instead of all 30 slipping through).
